prompt.context_jp: 院長の父に手をかけたのは自分ではないかという思い___、彼の胸を締めつけていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 院長の父に手をかけたのは自分ではないかという思い（　）、彼の胸を締めつけていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks this newly-introduced thought as what tightens his chest.

feedback.correct_en: The thought is newly introduced as the thing doing the 'tightening' — new-information subject, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the thought a pre-established topic, which clashes with it being newly presented here. を would require a transitive verb taking it as object.

contrast_examples.jp: その思いは今も消えない。
contrast_examples.en: That thought still doesn't fade. (established topic, は)

prompt.context_jp: 頭痛___ かなり良くなったよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭痛（　）かなり良くなったよ
prompt.prompt_en: Masakazu is giving an update on how his headaches are doing. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Headaches are the established topic of discussion — he's commenting on how that topic has changed, so は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 頭痛 as new information, as if announcing the headaches for the first time. を doesn't fit this intransitive comment.

contrast_examples.en: Has your fever gone down? (topic は)
A fever suddenly came on. (new event が)

prompt.context_jp: ちょうど廊下ですれ違ったの___、小野寺技師長だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ちょうど廊下ですれ違ったの（　）、小野寺技師長だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for this 'the one who X was Y' identification sentence.

feedback.correct_en: In a のは…だった cleft that identifies who it was, the のは frames the known situation as the topic, and the new identity follows. は is standard here.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが…だった is ungrammatical in this identificational cleft pattern; the の-nominalized clause takes は.

contrast_examples.jp: 最初に来たのは田中だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who came first was Tanaka.

prompt.context_jp: 最初に振り向いたの___悠木倫だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 最初に振り向いたの（　）悠木倫だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Identificational cleft — who was the first to turn around?

feedback.correct_en: The のは…だった pattern presents 'the one who turned around first' as the topic and identifies them as Yuki. は is required.
feedback.incorrect_en: が in this cleft would be ungrammatical; it would try to make the nominalized clause a new-info subject, which doesn't work here.

contrast_examples.en: The one who spoke is me.
I was the one who spoke. (exhaustive が)

prompt.context_jp: 私が技師になった頃ってさ 男___多くて
prompt.prompt_jp: 私が技師になった頃ってさ 男（　）多くて
prompt.prompt_en: Yuki describes what the workplace was like: 'there were lots of men.' Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: She's describing the makeup of the field — presenting 'men' as new information (existence/quantity description), so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 男は多くて would sound like contrasting men with something else as a known topic. に doesn't mark the subject of 多い.

contrast_examples.en: There are many kids in the park. (descriptive が)
Men are strong, women are kind. (contrast は)

prompt.context_jp: 僕が目指しているの___ 世界一の技師です
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕が目指しているの（　）世界一の技師です
prompt.prompt_en: 'What I'm aiming for is to be the world's best technician.' Pick the particle for this 'X is Y' statement.

feedback.correct_en: The のは…です pattern frames 'what I'm aiming for' as the topic and equates it with '世界一の技師'. This pseudo-cleft takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would try to present the nominalized clause as new-information subject, which doesn't fit the equative 'X=Y' structure.

contrast_examples.en: Health is the most important. (exhaustive が)

prompt.context_jp: あなた___ 罰せられるようなことを していない
prompt.prompt_jp: あなた（　）罰せられるようなことを していない
prompt.prompt_en: Nagisa reassures Igarashi: 'You haven't done anything that deserves punishment.' Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 'You' is the topic she's reassuring about — あなたは frames him as the subject of comment. Contrastive nuance also fits: 'you (in contrast to what they claim).'
feedback.incorrect_en: あなたが would exhaustively single out 'YOU are the one who hasn't...', which sounds like a rebuttal to 'who hasn't done it?' — not what the scene calls for.

contrast_examples.en: Was it you who did it? (identification が)

prompt.context_jp: 鏑木先生___ 頑張ってくれているから きっと 大丈夫
prompt.prompt_jp: 鏑木先生（　）頑張ってくれているから きっと 大丈夫
prompt.prompt_en: Nagisa reassures: 'Dr. Kaburagi is doing his best, so it'll be okay.' Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: も adds 'Dr. Kaburagi, too, is working hard' — implying additional support beyond what's already mentioned. The original script uses も here for that additive reassurance.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present him as the single new-info subject. は would make him the topic without the additive nuance of 'also pitching in.'

contrast_examples.jp: 田中さんも手伝ってくれる。
田中さんが手伝ってくれる。

prompt.context_jp: 僕___いなくなれば 甘春総合病院は また 元どおりになります
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕（　）いなくなれば 甘春総合病院は また 元どおりになります
prompt.prompt_en: 'If I disappear, the hospital will go back to normal.' Pick the particle for 僕 inside the conditional.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate conditional clause (〜ば), the subject typically takes が. The main-clause topic は is reserved for 甘春総合病院.
feedback.incorrect_en: 僕は...なれば sounds off because は generally doesn't mark subjects buried inside conditional clauses; it belongs to the main-clause topic.

contrast_examples.en: If it rains, we'll cancel. (subordinate が)

prompt.context_jp: これ以上 この病院___ 迷惑をかけるわけにいきません
prompt.prompt_jp: これ以上 この病院（　）迷惑をかけるわけにいきません
prompt.prompt_en: 'I can't cause any more trouble ___ this hospital.' Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 迷惑をかける takes に to mark the party that receives the trouble.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mean 'at the hospital (as location).' を already marks 迷惑 as object; the recipient takes に.

contrast_examples.jp: 学校で問題を起こした。
contrast_examples.en: I caused problems at school. (location で)

prompt.context_jp: 誰も___ずっと胸のどこかで抱いていた疑問だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰も（　）ずっと胸のどこかで抱いていた疑問だった。
prompt.prompt_en: 'It was a question that everyone had held in their hearts.' Pick the particle for 誰も.

feedback.correct_en: 誰もが means 'everyone (without exception)' as subject — a set expression using が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰もは is ungrammatical. 誰にも would mean 'to anyone,' changing the role.

prompt.context_jp: 僕___ 世界一の 放射線技師になるって決めたんです
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕（　）世界一の 放射線技師になるって決めたんです
prompt.prompt_en: Iori declares his life goal. Pick the particle for 僕.

feedback.correct_en: He's making a personal declaration about himself as a topic ('as for me, I decided...'), which takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 僕が would sound like he's identifying himself in contrast to others as the one who decided — not what this self-reflective statement needs.

contrast_examples.en: I'm going to be a doctor. (personal statement)

prompt.context_jp: 杏ちゃん 全然 覚えてなくて
prompt.prompt_jp: 杏ちゃん（　）全然 覚えてなくて
prompt.prompt_en: 'An doesn't remember at all (in contrast to me who does).' Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The contrastive は highlights An against Iori — 'I remember, but An doesn't.' That implicit contrast calls for は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 杏ちゃんが覚えてなくて would present An as new-info subject, missing the melancholy contrast that drives his line.

contrast_examples.jp: 私は覚えてるけど、彼女は忘れてる。
contrast_examples.en: I remember, but she's forgotten. (contrast は)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女が忘れてしまった。

prompt.context_jp: しかしその席の一つ___空いていることに、彼女はまだ気づいていない。
prompt.prompt_jp: しかしその席の一つ（　）空いていることに、彼女はまだ気づいていない。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for '(the fact) that one of the seats is empty.'

feedback.correct_en: Inside the こと-nominalized clause, the subject takes が. It's also new information about the state of the seats.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside こと-clauses sounds unnatural here. を doesn't fit intransitive 空いている.

contrast_examples.jp: 窓が開いていることに気づいた。
contrast_examples.en: I noticed the window was open.

contrast_examples.jp: その窓はもう閉まっている。
contrast_examples.en: That window is already closed. (main-clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: あいつさ ここ 辞めたんだよ
prompt.prompt_jp: あいつさ ここ（　）辞めたんだよ
prompt.prompt_en: 'He quit this place.' Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 辞める takes を to mark the job/place one leaves.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mean 'to here' (direction), で would mark location of action — neither matches 'quit.'

prompt.context_jp: 僕は あなたとの約束 守るために あなた___会いに来ました
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕は あなたとの約束 守るために あなた（　）会いに来ました
prompt.prompt_en: 'I came to see you.' Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 会う takes に to mark the person one meets.
feedback.incorrect_en: を with 会う is nonstandard. で marks location, not the meeting partner.

contrast_examples.en: We meet at the station. (location で)

prompt.context_jp: 自分の弱さを認める___をね
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の弱さを認める（　）をね
prompt.prompt_en: 'The ___ to acknowledge your own weakness.' Fill the blank.

feedback.correct_en: 勇気 (courage) collocates naturally with 認める — it takes courage to admit weakness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 元気 means 'energy/liveliness' and 人気 means 'popularity'; neither fits acknowledging weakness.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供は元気いっぱいだ。
contrast_examples.en: The child is full of energy.

prompt.context_jp: 申し訳ありません 僕を___ください
prompt.prompt_jp: 申し訳ありません 僕を（　）ください
prompt.prompt_en: Iori asks the director to let him go. Fill in the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 解雇する means 'to dismiss/fire (an employee)' — the request here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 解決する = resolve (a problem); 解散する = disband (a group). Neither applies to firing a person.

prompt.context_jp: もっと 経験を___ 知見を広げたいんです
prompt.prompt_jp: もっと 経験を（　）知見を広げたいんです
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the verb that collocates with 経験 ('experience').

feedback.correct_en: 経験を積む ('to accumulate experience') is the set collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 経験を作る/置く are not natural collocations in Japanese.

contrast_examples.en: To gain experience in the field.

prompt.context_jp: ああ もう 意志は___みたいだ
prompt.prompt_jp: ああ もう 意志は（　）みたいだ
prompt.prompt_en: 'His will seems ___.' Fill in the adjective.

feedback.correct_en: 意志が固い ('one's will is firm/resolute') is the standard set collocation for a firm resolve.
feedback.incorrect_en: 意志が強い exists but means 'strong-willed' as a trait; for 'his mind is made up' here, 固い is the idiomatic choice. 重い doesn't collocate with 意志.

contrast_examples.en: He is resolute/his mind is made up.

prompt.context_jp: ___もんかって思って 誰よりも 一生懸命 仕事した
prompt.prompt_jp: （　）もんかって思って 誰よりも 一生懸命 仕事した
prompt.prompt_en: 'I thought, I'm not going to ___!' Fill the verb for Yuki's defiant mindset.

feedback.correct_en: 負けるもんか ('like hell I'll lose!') is the defiant set phrase that matches her hard-working mindset.
feedback.incorrect_en: 勝つもんか ('I'll never win!') contradicts the determined tone. 止まるもんか doesn't fit the workplace rivalry context.

contrast_examples.jp: こんなことで負けるもんか。
contrast_examples.en: I'm not losing over something like this.

prompt.context_jp: 昔から 私の嫌な予感は ___んだよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 昔から 私の嫌な予感は（　）んだよ
prompt.prompt_en: 'My bad feelings always ___.' Fill the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 予感が当たる ('a hunch turns out to be right') is the standard collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 予感が合う / 着く are not idiomatic Japanese.

prompt.context_jp: 短い間でしたが ___になりました
prompt.prompt_jp: 短い間でしたが（　）になりました
prompt.prompt_en: Iori's farewell to his coworkers. Fill in the standard phrase.

feedback.correct_en: お世話になりました is the set departure/thank-you phrase meaning 'thank you for taking care of me.'
feedback.incorrect_en: お疲れさま and お元気で are separate phrases; neither fits the ___ になりました slot here.

contrast_examples.jp: 長い間お世話になりました。
contrast_examples.en: Thank you for all your help over the years.
Thanks for your hard work (end-of-day greeting).

prompt.context_jp: 私… 絶対に___から
prompt.prompt_jp: 私… 絶対に（　）から
prompt.prompt_en: An's declaration to Iori: 'I'll absolutely never ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 負けません ('I won't lose/be outdone') matches her follow-up about becoming a radiologist he can't interfere with.
feedback.incorrect_en: 忘れません and 行きません don't connect to the rivalry framing in her next line about becoming an excellent radiologist.

prompt.context_jp: An finally catches up to Iori at the bus stop and asks why he kept her in the dark.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for An's emotional question?

choices.text: どうして 言ってくれなかったんですか？
どうして 言わなかったですか？

feedback.correct_en: 〜てくれる conveys that she expected the favor of being told, and んですか seeks an explanation — both carry the emotional weight the scene needs.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言わなかったですか is grammatically awkward (plain past + ですか) and strips out the 〜てくれる nuance of expected consideration.

contrast_examples.jp: なんで教えてくれなかったんですか。
contrast_examples.en: Why didn't you tell me? (expecting the favor)

contrast_examples.jp: なんで教えなかったんですか。

prompt.context_jp: Director Masaichi thanks Iori for saving his daughter An.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural as a heartfelt thank-you?

choices.text: ありがとう 杏を助けてくれて
杏を助けた ありがとう

feedback.correct_en: ありがとう + 〜てくれて is the natural pattern for thanking someone for a specific action done on your behalf. Post-posing the reason after ありがとう also conveys warm emotion.
feedback.incorrect_en: '杏を助けた ありがとう' lacks the 〜てくれて that marks the action as a favor done for the speaker; it sounds flat and ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.jp: ありがとう、来てくれて。
手伝ってくれてありがとう。

prompt.context_jp: Director Omori asks about a promise with someone important. Iori responds.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Iori's reply?

choices.text: それを守るために行くんです
それを守るから行きます

feedback.correct_en: 〜ために expresses purpose ('in order to keep it'), and んです frames the trip as an explanation — exactly what this moment of revealing his reasons calls for.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜から行きます ('I'll go because I'll keep it') sounds like a loose causal statement and loses the purposive logic of 'leaving in order to keep the promise.'

contrast_examples.jp: 夢を叶えるために留学する。
contrast_examples.en: I'm studying abroad to achieve my dream.
I'm going home because I'm tired.

prompt.context_jp: Iori finally departs the radiology team with a formal goodbye.
prompt.prompt_en: Which closing fits best for leaving coworkers you expect to see again?

choices.text: ホントに お世話になりました いってきます
ホントに お世話になりました さようなら

feedback.correct_en: いってきます ('I'll be off and back') signals a departure with an implied return — matches his promise to come back. The scene shows him leaving but not severing ties.
feedback.incorrect_en: さようなら feels final, like a permanent goodbye — out of step with the hopeful 'see you again' tone the scene builds.

prompt.context_jp: Iori reflects after An's declaration at the bus stop.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'We just made a new promise.'?

choices.text: 今 新しい約束ができました
今 新しい約束を作りました

feedback.correct_en: 約束ができる ('a promise comes into being/forms') is the natural, slightly humble way to describe a promise that emerged between two people.
feedback.incorrect_en: 約束を作る sounds like manufacturing something; Japanese prefers する or できる for promises.
